content: Rumenic acid is a type of conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) that is predominantly found in the fat of ruminant animals and in dairy products derived from them. It is classified as an omega-7 trans fat. The chemical structure of rumenic acid is denoted as cis-9, trans-11 18:2 acid, which describes its specific arrangement of double bonds and carbon atoms. The term rumenic acid was introduced by Kramer and colleagues in 1998. This fatty acid is produced in the rumen of ruminant animals through a process called biohydrogenation, during which dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids are metabolized. Rumenic acid is formed alongside vaccenic acid during this process. It represents the primary form of CLA in the human diet, accounting for approximately 85-90% of the total CLA content found in dairy products. Experimental studies conducted in laboratory settings have demonstrated that rumenic acid exhibits anticarcinogenic properties, suggesting its potential role in inhibiting the development or progression of cancer.
